anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-level SQL or transaction design forces the engine to process more data, rows, or time than functionally required.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Concurrent sessions serialize on the same buffer pages, latches, or I/O slots, causing stalls and CPU spin without exhausting total memory.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : On-disk pages, index structures, or page links are physically or logically corrupt, making stored data structures unreliable.

When all three conditions coexist, the system is confronted with a mixed logical, concurrency, and physical failure mode. Long-running, data-heavy statements generated by sub-optimal workload logic pound a small set of hot tables and indexes. This concentrates traffic on a limited set of pages whose internal structures are already partially corrupt. Sessions therefore experience extreme and erratic latencies: extended runtime and timeouts from oversized scans, surges of buffer-busy and page-latch waits, sudden switch-overs to full table scans when index corruption is detected, duplicate or missing rows in result sets, increased deadlocks as transactions hold latches longer, intermittent checksum or page-verification errors, and a flood of retries or connection aborts at the application tier.

Causally, inefficient SQL drives excessive reads and writes against a narrow range of index and data pages, turning them into hotspots. The resulting latch pressure amplifies dwell time on those pages, magnifying the impact of any latent block or index corruption: corrupt pages are touched more often, triggering repeated checksum failures, forced page invalidations, or costly consistency checks. Conversely, corruption can invalidate index access paths, forcing the optimizer to fall back to full scans that exacerbate the already heavy workload, further swelling the buffer churn and latch queues. The feedback loop between bad SQL patterns, contention for shared buffers, and structural corruption degrades throughput, increases error rates, and can ultimately lead to service outages or emergency recovery operations.

entry.error_class: Class 42 - Syntax Error or Access Rule Violation
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with unsupported syntax, invalid statement structure, or feature usage that the target engine version cannot execute as written.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate SQL syntax, target-engine compatibility, statement shape, and whether the feature is supported under the current engine version or execution context.
